A survey from YouGov/Economist released on Tuesday shows that in a generic congressional vote, 36 percent of U.S. adults would pick the Democratic candidate compared to 31 percent who would pick the Republican candidate. One percent said other, eight percent said not sure and 23 percent said they would not vote.

The poll surveyed 1,592 U.S. adults from August 28-31 and had a margin of error of 3.5 percent. [...] During the second quarter of 2026, 49 percent of Americans identified as Democrats or leaned toward the Democratic Party, compared to 39 percent who identified as Republicans or leaned Republican, according to the data.
